text:
maria: Hey team, ran a cross-region kernel/binary sweep for the q5_k-quantized llm-13b today. Saw a weird pattern: FlashV3 is much faster on short sequences in us-west but regresses on long contexts in eu-west vs Triton vendor kernel.

soham: Can you paste the microbench commands + outputs?

maria: Sure — ran the standard bench harness on dedicated nodes (h100 L40 in us-west, h100 L40 variant in eu-west with slightly older driver). Commands:
```
./bench --model llm-13b-q5 --kernels flashv3,triton --region us-west --seq-lens 8,512 --batch 4 --warmup 200 --iter 100
./bench --model llm-13b-q5 --kernels flashv3,triton --region eu-west --seq-lens 8,512 --batch 4 --warmup 200 --iter 100
```
Raw (median) numbers:
us-west:
- flashv3 short 8: 11.8 ms / tok
- flashv3 long 512: 195 ms / seq
- triton short 8: 16.4 ms / tok
- triton long 512: 210 ms / seq

eu-west:
- flashv3 short 8: 13.1 ms / tok
- flashv3 long 512: 230 ms / seq  <-- 17% worse
- triton short 8: 18.0 ms / tok
- triton long 512: 198 ms / seq  <-- triton wins on long here

jen: Interesting. Driver versions differ? FlashV3 is sensitive to kernel-launch latency and driver ABI.

maria: eu-west nodes are on driver 535.x, us-west on 550.x. We also saw higher p99 jitter in eu-west when switching kernels at runtime (fallbacks kicking in).

alex: Do you see KV cache eviction or packing differences? q5_k layout can change memory access pattern.

maria: Yes — KV cache footprint similar, but profiling shows more kernel thrash: small short-seq requests are causing frequent kernel rebinds on FlashV3 under the older driver. The tracer shows extra memcpy calls before the matmul for long sequences.

eval-bot: Quality check: generation cross-entropy delta between flashv3/triton on q5_k is <0.2% on our eval set — no substantial quality regression.

soham: Hypothesis: older driver + FlashV3 kernel selection path triggers a slower long-path (maybe non-fused attention variant). Quick reproducer: run with env var FF_KERNEL_DEBUG=1 and capture which kernel names are chosen.

maria: Ran that. On eu-west FlashV3 picks `attn_fused_v3_split` for long seqs while us-west used `attn_fused_v3_nopack` (different heuristics). The split path does extra gather-scatter steps.

jen: Ops implication: For Dedicated customers in eu-west we may want runtime routing policy: prefer Triton for >256 tokens until we fix the driver/kernel mismatch. We can do a canary with 5% traffic.

alex: Also try forcing `FLASHV3_FORCE_PACK=1` — packing sometimes reduces kernel-launch overhead for short batches.

maria: Tested FORCE_PACK: short seq latency increased slightly (pack overhead), but long seq improved ~8% — that narrows the gap vs Triton. Full results attached in gist: https://gist.redwood/bench-2219876543

infra-bot: Suggested action:
- create canary route for region eu-west: kernel_preference=[triton,flashv3] for seq>256
- schedule driver upgrade on eu-west test fleet
- add kernel-selection logging to 1% of prod requests

soham: Also file for attention-kernel upstream: pass the `attn_fused_v3_split` stacktrace to vendor; they might have a microkernel patch for older drivers.

jen: TL;DR / action items:
1) Canary routing (eu-west) preferring Triton for >256 tokens (Soham + Infra)
2) Driver upgrade on a subset of eu-west test nodes (Infra)
3) Kernel selection debug logs enabled for 1% (MLOps)
4) Re-run quantized bench after driver roll (Maria)

maria: I'll open a PR with the canary config and attach the bench CSVs.

alex: Thanks — this explains why our switchover heuristics were flaky across regions. Nice find.

maria: :thumbsup: I'll ping when PR is up and when eu-west test driver is live.
